grammar.title: Past Continuous and Past Simple
grammar.explanation:
We use the **past continuous** for an action in progress in the past. We make it with **was / were + verb-ing**.

Use **was** with I, he, she, and it. Use **were** with you, we, and they.

The **past continuous** is the long background action. The **past simple** is the short action in the middle of it.

Use **when** before the short action. Use **while** before the long action.

For negatives, use **wasn't** or **weren't**. For questions, put **was** or **were** first.
examples: *At 7 o'clock this morning, I **was having** breakfast. (in progress at a time)
*They **were playing** football when it **started** to snow. (interrupted action)
*While we **were waiting** for the bus, we **saw** an accident. (while + long action)
*She **wasn't wearing** a coat, so she was cold. (negative)
*I **was reading** while my brother **was cooking**. (two actions at the same time)
